deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is working material for Riemann's 1861 paper 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines gleichartigen flüssigen Ellipsoides'. That paper treats self-gravitating homogeneous ellipsoids in stationary motion (the Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann problem). Here a, b, c are semi-axes. τ and τ' are the two rotation/vorticity parameters. H is (up to normalisation) the gravitational potential-energy function of the shape. The next page (heat conduction in a sphere) is unrelated.

(1) Conditions for stationary figures (top left). Riemann writes
  4τ²/(b−a)^k = −(1/b)∂H/∂m + (1/a)∂H/∂n,
  τ'²/(b+a)^k = −(1/b)∂H/∂m − (1/a)∂H/∂n.
Here m, n are logarithmic shape variables, with ∂b/∂m = b.
- The side note (b−a)³+(b+a)³ = 2b(b²+3a²) [completion mine] shows the denominators must effectively be cubes. Only then do the next lines follow.
- Adding and subtracting gives
  ab(τ²+τ'²) = −ab(b²+3a²)H_m − ab(3b²+a²)H_n,
  ab(τ²−τ'²) = −a²(3b²+a²)H_m − b²(b²+3a²)H_n,
  both up to an overall constant factor.

(2) Shape coordinates. Volume is constant: a²b²c² = (β²−α²)b⁶ = const. Set a² = b²(β+α) and c² = b²(β−α), so b = const·(β²−α²)^{−1/6} and a = b(β+α)^{1/2}. Thus β = (a²+c²)/(2b²) and α = (a²−c²)/(2b²); small β is a needle elongated along the b-axis.
- Put H = y/b, so H_m = (y_m − y)/b and H_n = y_n/b. This gives
  −(τ²+τ'²) = b[(1+3(β+α))(y_m−y) + (3+β+α)y_n],
  −(τ²−τ'²) = (b²/a)[(β+α)(3+β+α)(y_m−y) + (1+3(β+α))y_n].
- Change to variables p, q with y_n = y_q and y_m = ½(y_p+y_q). The brackets become one half of
  (1+3(β+α))(y_p−2y) + (7+5(β+α))y_q,
  (β+α)(3+β+α)(y_p−2y) + (2+9(β+α)+(β+α)²)y_q.
- These are called ψ and φ, with prefactors b = (β²−α²)^{−1/6} and b²/a = (β+α)^{−2/3}(β−α)^{−1/6}.
- The operators are ∂/∂p = −3(α∂_α + β∂_β) (a dilation) and ∂/∂q = β∂_α + α∂_β (a hyperbolic rotation preserving β²−α²).

(3) Derivatives of the full quantities Ψ = (β²−α²)^{−1/6}ψ and Φ = (β+α)^{−2/3}(β−α)^{−1/6}φ, multiplied by (β²−α²)^{7/6} etc.
- (β²−α²)ψ_α + ⅓αψ and (β²−α²)ψ_β − ⅓βψ.
- The logarithmic derivative of the φ-prefactor is −(2/3)/(β+α) + (1/6)/(β−α). This gives (β²−α²)φ_α + (5/6 α − ½β)φ and (β²−α²)φ_β + (½α − 5/6 β)φ. The scratch '−4β+4α+β+α' is six times the α-coefficient.
- Sums and differences divided by (β∓α): (β+α)(ψ_α+ψ_β) − ⅓ψ; (β−α)(ψ_α−ψ_β) + ⅓ψ; (β+α)(φ_α+φ_β) − (4/3)φ; (β−α)(φ_α−φ_β) + ⅓φ.
- In p, q form: βψ_α + αψ_β; αψ_α + βψ_β − ⅓ψ; and analogously for φ with −(5/3)φ.
- He then assembles a Jacobian-type expression (β²−α²)·2(ψ_βφ_α − φ_βψ_α) plus lower terms, i.e. essentially ∂(Ψ,Φ)/∂(α,β).
- Plausible purpose (my interpretation): find where the map shape ↦ (τ²+τ'², τ²−τ'²) degenerates, i.e. fold or boundary curves of the family of stationary figures. This is relevant to the existence and stability discussion of the paper.

(4) Series ansatz near the needle. y = f(β) + α²f''(β)/16 + α⁴f''''(β)/(16·36), i.e. even in α.
- y_p − 2y = −2y − 3(αy_α + βy_β) = −2f − 2α²f''/16 − 2α⁴f''''/576 − 6α²f''/16 − 12α⁴f''''/576 − 3βf' − 3α²βf'''/16 − 3α⁴βf^V/576.
- y_q = α[2βf''/16 + 4α²βf''''/576 + f' + α²f'''/16 + …].
- Substituting and sorting by powers of α:
  ψ_0 = (1+3β)(−2f − 3βf'),
  ψ_1 = α[(coefficient)(−2f − 3βf') + (7+5β)(f' + βf''/8)],
  ψ_2 = α²[(−½f'' − (3/16)βf''')(1+3β) + 5(f' + βf''/8)],
  ψ_3 = α³[… + (7+5β)(f'''/16 + βf''''/144)].
  The φ expansion is begun similarly.

(5) Specialisation f(β) = log(β/4), with f' = 1/β, f'' = −1/β², f''' = 2/β³, f'''' = −6/β⁴. This is the leading needle asymptotics of the potential, since b·∫ds/√((a²+s)(b²+s)(c²+s)) ≈ −log(a²/4b²) for a = c ≪ b.
- Leading terms for small β: ψ ≈ −2log(β/4) − 3 + 7·(7/8)α/β + (½ − 3/8)α²/β² + 7(1/8 − 1/24)α³/β³ = −2log(β/4) − 3 + (49/8)α/β + (1/8)α²/β² + (7/12)α³/β³.
- For φ: φ ≈ 3β(−2log(β/4) − 3) + 2·(7/8)α/β + ….
- Setting φ = 0 at leading order gives the curve α = (12/7)β²(2log(β/4) + 3).
- The bottom-right lines are further trial expansions: 49/8 + ¼α/β; −2α/β − (49/8)α²/β²; 7/4 − (7/8)α/β + (3/2)α²/β²; 3β(−4log(β/4)) + (5·7/4)α/β + (5/6)α²/β². They are too fragmentary to reconstruct reliably.

(6) Side calculation (lower left): derivatives of √(1−β)·logβ.
- First derivative: √(1−β)/β − ½(1−β)^{−1/2}logβ.
- Second derivative, expanded near β = 0: −1/β² − 1/(2β) − ¼(1−β)^{−3/2}logβ.
- This apparently tests a candidate f with a logarithmic singularity.
errors: As transcribed, the first two equations have squares (b∓a)² in the denominators and a factor 4 only on τ². The sum and difference lines (b²+3a², 3b²+a²) only follow with cubes (b∓a)³ and the same factor on both. The side note (b−a)³+(b+a)³ confirms cubes were intended. Overall constant factors and the sign of the τ²−τ'² line are not consistent with the equations as transcribed (one gets +a²(3b²+a²)H_m + b²(b²+3a²)H_n up to a constant). This is probably a labelling or normalisation slip or a misreading.

In the line '5α∂y/∂q + (1+3β)(y_p−2y) + (α(y_p−2y) + (7+5β)y_q)' and in the ψ-block α and α³ rows, the coefficient multiplying α(y_p−2y) should be 3, from 1+3(β+α). As written it appears as 1. The error does not affect the leading small-β coefficients 49/8 and 1/8.

The expansion of the φ-coefficients is inconsistent. From (β+α)(3+β+α) and 2+9(β+α)+(β+α)² one gets α(3+2β)(y_p−2y) and α(9+2β)y_q. The page shows '3α(1+4β)y_q', '+6α²' and '3(1+β+2β²)' in the φ block. The transcription's 4(β+α)² is likely a misreading of (β+α)², since the derivation gives (β+α)².

The ansatz coefficients 1/16 and 1/(16·36) do not reproduce the needle potential −log((β+√(β²−α²))/2), whose series is f + α²f''/4 + α⁴f''''/64. Either y is normalised differently (e.g. a rescaled α) or the ansatz solves a different equation. I cannot confirm its exactness from this page.
In ∂y/∂p − 2y the third line omits the α², α⁴ factors on the f''' and f^V terms (shorthand, harmless).

results.what: Rewriting the stationarity conditions for rotating homogeneous ellipsoids (τ, τ' vs derivatives of the potential function) in volume-preserving coordinates α, β with a² = b²(β+α), c² = b²(β−α), b ∝ (β²−α²)^{-1/6}
results.modern_name: Riemann ellipsoids: equilibrium conditions of the Dirichlet–Dedekind–Riemann problem

results.what: Jacobian-type combination of the two condition functions Ψ, Φ, used to locate degeneracies of the map from shapes to (τ², τ'²)
results.modern_name: Fold/boundary analysis of the equilibrium family (related to Riemann's stability discussion)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 (stability section); Lebovitz, Chandrasekhar in modern form

results.what: Asymptotic expansion near the needle limit with f = log(β/4), giving ψ ≈ −2log(β/4) − 3 + (49/8)α/β + (1/8)α²/β² and the curve α ≈ (12/7)β²(2log(β/4)+3) from φ = 0
results.modern_name: Asymptotics of the ellipsoid potential (elliptic integrals) for very elongated shapes
results.usually_credited_to: standard in potential theory of ellipsoids (Dirichlet, Riemann, later Chandrasekhar)

deep.surprise_reason: Scratch computations supporting Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid paper: coordinate change, derivative bookkeeping and a needle-limit asymptotic expansion. The details are unpublished but contain no result beyond what is known to be his work on Riemann ellipsoids.

leading α/β coefficient of ψ is 49/8
leading α²/β² coefficient of ψ is 1/8 (½ − 3/8)
leading α³/β³ coefficient of ψ is 7(1/8 − 1/24) = 7/12

transcription_corrections: 'a²α²b² = (β²−α²)b⁶ = const' should read a²c²b² = (β²−α²)b⁶ = const (volume constraint).

In ∂y/∂q and in the ψ block, 'f'''(β)' in the terms 2f''β/16 and (1/8)f''β should be f''(β), and 'f^V' in 4α²f^{IV}β/(16·36) and f^{IV}β/(16·9) should be f^{IV}. This is required by β·∂_α of the ansatz.
'(2+9(β+α)+4(β+α)²)' should be (2+9(β+α)+(β+α)²), as the derivation requires.
'∂H/∂m = (1/b)(∂y/∂m − y)' is consistent with H = y/b and ∂b/∂m = b; the transcription is fine there.
Denominators in the first two lines are probably (b−a)³ and (b+a)³ rather than squares, given the side note (b−a)³+(b+a)³.
